title: [Feature Request] option to execute klipper action commands without using the shell /bin/sh
line: Klipper action commands can now be run without a shell, with each inserted clipboard text passed as a single argument.
explanation: Klipper always ran action commands with QProcess::setShellCommand, after shell-quoting %s and %0–%9 through KMacroExpander, so the clipboard text's safety rested entirely on that quoting and /bin/sh's parsing; the dialog didn't say so or warn about texts starting with a dash. The Command Properties dialog now has a "Run the command in a shell" checkbox (on by default, so existing commands behave as before, saved as UseShell). When it is off, the command line is split into arguments with KShell::splitArgs and %s/%N are expanded inside each argument without quoting, then run with QProcess program + arguments, so an inserted text is always exactly one argument. The hint also suggests putting -- before the inserted texts.

commits.message:
klipper: add an option to run action commands without a shell

Action commands always ran through /bin/sh, relying on quoting to keep
the clipboard text safe. A per-command checkbox now runs them directly
with each inserted text as one argument, and the hint suggests "--".

BUG: 527863

media.caption: Command Properties on master: no way to avoid the shell, and nothing about it in the hint
New "Run the command in a shell" checkbox with its hint, and the -- advice in the main hint
Master, same three commands on "hello world": the command marked no-shell still went through the shell (HELLO WORLD)
With the fix: shell gives HELLO WORLD, no-shell passes "| tr a-z A-Z" literally to echo, and printf '[%%s]' %s gives one argument: [hello world]
